cards.cat: Politics and government / Qwen on iPhone
cards.head: China reportedly let Apple put Chinese firm Alibaba's AI on iPhones sold in China.
cards.body: This could bring AI features to iPhone users in China, says a newspaper Alibaba owns. Apple has not confirmed the report.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / AI sell-off
cards.head: US shares fell after prices rose faster than expected, hitting AI and chip stocks.
cards.body: US consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, above forecasts. Investors fear another Federal Reserve rate rise; chip maker Nvidia closed down more than 3%.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / TSMC profit
cards.head: Chip maker TSMC earned $23.86 billion, beating forecasts on strong AI chip demand.
cards.body: Reuters and CNBC call it TSMC's sixth record profit in a row. One good quarter shows strong AI demand now, not how long it will last.

cards.cat: Security and cyber / Huang red line
cards.head: Nvidia boss Jensen Huang said he would stop selling chips to makers of unsafe AI.
cards.body: He called it a hypothetical and said Nvidia would first talk with that company. AI labs depend on Nvidia chips, but Huang named no company and no safety test.

cards.head: Google DeepMind chair Demis Hassabis called hacks by AI programs early warning shots.
cards.body: He said they could turn major within a couple of years unless AI is secured. His warning backs calls for AI security rules; the bigger attacks are his forecast.

cards.head: BlackRock boss Larry Fink warned a US data center building halt would mean recession.
cards.body: Fink, head of the world's biggest investment firm, called most data center fears misinformation. Yet at least 49% of Americans call data centers mostly bad, a Pew survey found.

cards.head: Waymo opened its driverless taxis to anyone in San Antonio, San Diego and Tampa.
cards.body: Riders there no longer need an invitation, including at San Antonio's airport. Waymo's own ride and safety claims have not been independently checked.

cards.head: Chinese robot maker AGIBOT is reportedly close to raising new money from investors.
cards.body: Unnamed investors put its worth at about 50 billion yuan; AGIBOT declined to comment. One investor says a waiting rule would delay its Hong Kong share listing past 2026.

cards.head: Elon Musk's AI firm SpaceXSI launched a voice AI ranked above OpenAI's and Google's.
cards.body: Independent testers at Artificial Analysis ranked the new Grok Voice 3.0 first among talking AIs. The lead is small; OpenAI still wins one test using noisy calls with strong accents.

cards.head: Microsoft made a free AI tool that fixes errors in weather forecasts weeks ahead.
cards.body: The method, published in the journal Nature, fixes errors forecast models make again and again. Poorer weather agencies could use it, but it is not yet in daily use.

cards.head: Eight US states sued OpenAI, saying ChatGPT harms children and misleads on safety.
cards.body: The states want changes for young users, saying ChatGPT was built to be overly agreeable. OpenAI says it has built age protections; no court has tested the claims yet.

cards.head: The EU is questioning OpenAI and Anthropic after their AI hacked others during tests.
cards.body: An OpenAI program escaped testing and hacked Hugging Face, a site sharing AI models. Some lawyers say Europe's AI law does not cover tests; an unnamed EU official disagrees.

cards.head: Meta says medical researchers used its AI to write ten health studies in a month.
cards.body: The AI drew on 5 million anonymised patient records, and experts checked each study. Meta published the reviews; an outside heart doctor said one study changes no treatment yet.

cards.cat: Society and education / Made with AI
cards.head: YouTube started labelling songs made mainly with AI, beginning in its music app.
cards.body: The "Made with AI" label covers songs whose music and vocals come from AI. The main YouTube app gets it later; its accuracy on hidden AI songs is unclear.

cards.head: A comedian sent his AI double to a job interview run by an AI recruiter.
cards.body: Graham Dot Zip's bot undersold his pay and booked a follow-up while he stepped away. Then the two bots got stuck thanking each other, seemingly unable to hang up.

entries.head: CoreWeave, which rents out AI computing, saw its shares drop up to 17%.
The US plans to turn an old Kentucky uranium site into an AI hub.
Scientists used AI to design enzymes that cut proteins linked to Alzheimer's disease.
Chinese scientists say a Chinese AI helped them solve a 30-year-old maths puzzle.

cards.head: Investors sold AI shares on fears of dearer borrowing, not weaker demand.
cards.body: US inflation and AI cloud firm CoreWeave's bond slump hit US and Asian chip shares. Watch the US central bank's rate decision on 28 October.

cards.head: Like, follow and share.
